body.text: Which Aegean hubs (İzmir, Aydın, Manisa, Ayvalık) lead in private-label olive oil, figs and hazelnuts?

İzmir serves as the primary export, bottling, and port hub, while Aydın dominates dried fig processing and Manisa leads in seedless sultanas. North along the coast, Ayvalık produces aromatic early-harvest olive oils. Although commercial hazelnuts grow along the Black Sea, several İzmir packers roast and private-label hazelnut spreads alongside Aegean pantry lines.

Regional export coordination runs through the [Aegean Exporters' Associations (EİB)](https://en.eib.org.tr/Sayfa.Asp?SI_Id=F1615468AE) in İzmir, including the [Aegean Olive and Olive Oil Exporters' Association](https://www.olivetolive.com/en/about-us.aspx), whose members ship to over 130 countries. Geographical indications tracked by the [Turkish Patent and Trademark Office (TÜRKPATENT)](https://www.turkpatent.gov.tr/en/news/edremit-zeytinyagi-olive-oil-and-aydin-memecik-zeytinyagi-olive-oil-expand-into-global-markets) protect EU-registered origins such as Aydın İnciri (dried fig), Aydın Memecik Zeytinyağı, and Edremit Zeytinyağı, alongside nationally registered Ayvalık olive oil.

body.text: What EU/US FDA food-export compliance and lab tests are required?

Exporting Aegean foods to the EU or US requires BRCGS Food or IFS certification, accredited lab testing, and mycotoxin screening. Dried figs entering Europe face strict aflatoxin and ochratoxin A checks tracked via [EU RASFF](https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/screen/notification/873981), while US imports require [FDA Prior Notice](https://www.fda.gov/industry/fda-import-process/prior-notice-imported-foods), facility registration, and importer [FSVP verification](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-modernization-act-fsma/fsma-final-rule-foreign-supplier-verification-programs-fsvp-importers-food-humans-and-animals).

items: Mycotoxin & residue labs: Require ISO/IEC 17025 accredited lab reports per lot for aflatoxin B1/total aflatoxins, ochratoxin A, and multi-residue pesticides.
Olive oil authenticity: Check free fatty acidity (<=0.8% for extra virgin), peroxide value, UV spectrophotometry (K232/K270), and sensory panel scores.
Physical & UV sorting: Audit handheld or inline UV fluorescence (BGYF) fig-sorting rooms, X-ray or metal detection, and cold-storage humidity controls.

Non-legal/non-broker scope: Itinerary of Türkiye coordinates factory visits, schedules, and independent introductions; contracts, customs clearance, phytosanitary filings, FDA/EU compliance, and legal or tax due diligence belong strictly to licensed Turkish customs brokers, attorneys, and official authorities.

body.text: When is the best harvest season to visit mills and packers?

Visit Aydın fig packers and Manisa raisin processors between mid-September and November, right as the new crop enters UV sorting, washing, and export packing lines. For olive oil, late October through December lets buyers taste fresh early-harvest pressings at Ayvalık and İzmir mills before bulk contracts lock up the best single-estate lots.

Spring visits (March to May) still work well for private-label label design, bottle tooling, and secondary food-safety audits, though olive mills will be idle and buyers will evaluate tank-stored oil rather than live decanters.
How do you combine sourcing with Urla or İzmir stays?

Fly into [İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport (ADB)](https://izmirairport.com/en) and base yourself either in central İzmir (Konak or Alsancak) for fast highway access to Manisa and Aydın, or 45 minutes west on the Urla peninsula for quiet boutique hotels and vineyard dinners after full plant-audit days.

A three-day circuit covers İzmir and Manisa on Day 1, Aydın fig packers on Day 2, and a northern loop to Ayvalık olive mills on Day 3—easily paired with Marmara hubs like [Bursa](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa) on the same trip. faq.q: Can private-label buyers source retail-ready glass jars and tins directly in İzmir?
faq.a: Yes. Export-oriented İzmir and Ayvalık packers offer turnkey bottling in dark glass, tin cans, and stand-up pouches with your retail barcodes and multilingual labels, subject to per-SKU minimum order quantities.

faq.q: Why are EU border checks strict on Turkish dried figs?
faq.a: Warm harvest conditions can trigger aflatoxin or ochratoxin A formation in dried figs. Buyers should verify that packers run strict UV fluorescence sorting and pre-shipment ISO 17025 lab testing on every export lot.

faq.q: Where are Türkiye's main hazelnut orchards if I want to source hazelnuts too?
faq.a: Commercial hazelnut orchards lie along the Black Sea coast (Ordu, Giresun, Sakarya), though several İzmir specialty-food packers process roasted hazelnuts, spreads, and mixed-nut packs for consolidated Aegean containers.

faq.q: How long does an Aegean olive oil and dried fruit sourcing trip take?
faq.a: Plan three working days for İzmir, Aydın, and Manisa, or four days if adding Ayvalık olive mills and a relaxed evening stay in Urla.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye inspect lab certificates or clear food shipments through customs?
faq.a: No. We coordinate independent visit itineraries, transport, and factory introductions. Lab verification, export health certificates, FDA/EU filings, and customs clearance are handled by accredited labs, licensed customs brokers, and attorneys.

faq.q: Are organic (EU Organic / USDA NOP) olive oils and dried figs available in the Aegean?
faq.a: Yes. Aydın, Manisa, and İzmir host numerous certified organic packers; always inspect current scope certificates and verify transaction-certificate workflows with your certifying body before ordering.
